delay_description: Other prerequisite — blocking event must resolve

trigger_phrases.phrase: Renovation, refurbishment, or building work not yet complete
Mortgage/financing structure or lender terms not yet resolved
Third-party consent required (freeholder, management company, or existing letting agent)
Compliance, certification, or legal-permission requirement (gas/electrical certs, change of use, subletting clause, short-let licence)
Lead's own travel or personal logistics gate when they can act
Wants to inspect the property or receive written materials before deciding
Current cost base doesn't yet justify switching — needs the numbers to improve first
Probate/inheritance process not yet complete — no legal possession of the property
Building/lease ultimately found not to permit short-letting — discovered after the sales call, not screened for beforehand

typical_timeline.notes: This category spans the widest range of blockers — from a same-week spousal sign-off to multi-month renovation, mortgage-restructuring, or third-party consent processes — so no single timeframe dominates; most named timelines resolved within one to three months. A subset (building/lease eligibility) is not a timing delay at all but a hard-stop discovered too late in the pipeline.

what_leads_focus_on_while_waiting.concern: When the builder/renovation/refurb will actually finish
Sorting mortgage rate, lender permission, or funding structure
Getting sign-off from a freeholder, management company, or existing letting agent
Bringing a partner or spouse up to speed before committing jointly
Confirming legal/compliance requirements are met (certificates, change of use, mortgage T&Cs, short-let licence)
Wanting to see the property or written materials in hand before deciding
Awaiting probate/legal possession of an inherited property
Whether the building/lease itself permits short-letting at all — surfacing only after commercial terms were already agreed

how_to_handle_in_meeting.acknowledge_phrase: What I'll do is I'll share my screen and we can go through what we've estimated, the projections are and also where I think the gaps are as well.
how_to_handle_in_meeting.timeline_question: Of everything still to sort before this could go live — [the specific blocker named] — what's the realistic next milestone, and when do you expect to know more?
how_to_handle_in_meeting.reframe_approach: Because this category covers genuinely different blockers, name the specific one back to the lead precisely (builder, lender, freeholder, spouse, certificate) rather than treating it as generic hesitation, and address it on its own terms.
how_to_handle_in_meeting.how_to_keep_engaged: Give the lead something concrete to act on or forward — a written summary, action plan, or case study — so waiting on the third party (partner, freeholder, lender, agent) still moves the decision forward, and let the lead set the follow-up date once they've named their own trigger.
how_to_handle_in_meeting.what_to_write_to_monday: Log the specific blocking event in plain terms (which renovation stage, which third party's consent, which document the spouse is reviewing) and the date it's expected to resolve, since 'other' blockers need their own description to be useful later. For leasehold/managed-building properties, explicitly confirm building/lease permission for short-letting BEFORE agreeing commercial terms — two lost deals this run (092, 094) reached offer/onboarding stage before this was discovered.

conversion_after_delay.drop_off_reason: Decided to long let property; Building does not allow

do_not_attempt_offer_because: The blocker sits with a party or process outside the lead's direct control (a builder, a lender, a freeholder, a spouse who wasn't on the call), so a signing deadline created by Stayful cannot force that third party to move faster, and risks pressuring the lead into a commitment they cannot yet honour. Where the blocker is building/lease eligibility itself, no offer should be made or agreement signed until permission is confirmed in writing.
